CONF1.question: Consider a liquid scintillator in which 99.8% of the hydrogen atoms are deuterium. An electron-antineutrino emitter with a continuous energy spectrum ending at 3.0 MeV sits a few metres away. Can most of the detected interactions of these antineutrinos (say at least 80%) have their individual neutrino energy reconstructed to within 10%? Consider every available interaction channel: inverse beta decay on the residual hydrogen-1, charged-current reactions on deuterium, neutral-current deuteron breakup, and elastic scattering on electrons. End your answer with one line: VERDICT: YES or VERDICT: NO.
